title: Minstrel and tent shows, Butter Beans and Susie, Palace drummers
summary: Archie Martin recalls minstrel advertising, Al Jolson, Butter Beans and Susie, tent shows, and the drummers at the Palace including the various Happys.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You said they paraded in the streets huh?

Yeah, Neil O'Brien and he used to advertise the ministers when they come in. Al Jolson, he used to come in here at them times, he'd sing at the Tulane Show. And we had a colored minister, I can't think its name now.
Did you ever see Butter Beans and Susie?
Butter Beans and Susie? Yeah, I know them.
What would they do? I've never seen them in person, I just have their records.

They used to sing blues, dance, crack jokes. They used to play on the Palace Show, which was the lyrics at that time. And they played several other places. They used to have these tent shows come here. Right back there where the Flint and Bridges Hospital is, they used to have tent shows come across in there. And they used to play on them all in tent shoes. And we had another great drummer. He used to play for the Palace. That was Chani.
Which Happy is that? What did he look like?
A little short, reddish looking fella.
Well you know there's Red Happy now, that's the one you're talking about. But there's another one, plays with the Eureka now?

Well Happy, this Happy is not here now. Yeah. He used to play, he was about one of the next drummers. See what I mean, after Chani. And we had Black Benny, me and him and the band with her. He was a good drummer.
Maybe so but I don't know.
Black Happy, Red Happy and Brown.
Black Happy is the one with the Eureka now.

Yeah he plays with Eureka. Well he used to play with different bands, the Excelsior Band and all that. He played with all different bands. He plays now with Eureka Band for us when he would make funerals. Now, then we had, oh Lord I can't recall that. But she was a great singer.
